title: Failure Spectrograph: unified trace-hook adapter and error taxonomy dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a unified failure "spectrograph" that combines tracing-hooks, normalized error taxonomy (timeouts, overloads, model-layer errors, HTTP/gRPC codes), and a set of operational dashboards and pipelines. The goal is to make incident triage 2x faster by surfacing root cause signals, recommended remediation playbooks, and correlated KPI trends (p50/p95 latency, error-rate by model variant, capacity pressure). Deliverables: trace-hook adapter, log/metric enrichment pipeline schema, three dashboards (overview, model-error drilldown, overload/timeouts heatmap), alert rule recommendations, and rollout plan for sample-rate changes.
acceptance_criteria: Trace-hook adapter deployed to runtime staging that attaches standardized failure attributes to spans (failure_type, failure_subtype, model_variant, capacity_signal)
Ingestion pipeline transforms logs and metrics into the new schema and populates the observability cluster (ES or OLAP) with <24h latency
Overview dashboard shows grouped failure counts by category and top contributing services for past 7d with links to traces
Model-error drilldown dashboard shows token-level failure patterns and correlations with model version and sequence length
Overload/timeouts heatmap surfaces host and queue pressure over time with ability to filter by region and capacity tier
Runbook for each top-level failure_type with suggested first steps and automated playbook links available from the dashboard
No customer-facing latency regressions in runtime (perf regression <2% in staging smoke tests)
technical_notes: Failure taxonomy derives from: TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_REJECT, MODEL_RUNTIME_ERROR, HTTP_4xx, HTTP_5xx, GRPC_CANCELLED, GRPC_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
Trace-hook will enrich spans at three points: request ingress, model dispatch, response emission. Add KV keys: failure_type, failure_code, model_variant, queue_wait_ms, kernel_fallback
Use sampler that biases high-error-rate routes and high-latency traces (score = error*5 + latency_ratio*2) to keep storage costs bounded
Log pipeline mapping: raw_error_message -> normalized_failure_code using regex rules; emit both raw and normalized fields to preserve fidelity
Dashboards implemented in Grafana using pre-aggregated OLAP tables (hourly rollups) + live rollup for 1h window
Plan to utilize existing trace enrichment lambda from ENG-7246 with minor adapter layer to avoid duplicated parsing work
decision_log: 2025-01-17: Chose taxonomy that distinguishes 'MODEL_REJECT' (model returns intentional rejection token) from 'MODEL_RUNTIME_ERROR' (runtime exception). Rationale: different remediation steps and SLA exposure.
2025-01-22: Decided to implement enrichment at the runtime boundary instead of downstream agent to get queue_wait_ms reliably. Trade-off: small change in runtime vs more accurate signal.
2025-01-28: Agreed on sampling strategy to reduce cost: adaptive sampling that scales with error rate and latency. Remaining action: produce knob in Console to tune sample targets per-customer.
2025-02-05: Opted for Grafana/OLAP backed dashboards instead of raw Kibana dashboards for faster multi-dim slicing. Implementation notes recorded in Confluence.
2025-02-08: Security review: no PII fields added to spans; normalized_failure_code is low-sensitivity. Flagged future review if raw_error_message is included in exports.
2025-02-09: Rollout strategy approved: feature-flagged staging -> internal -> canary 1% -> 10% -> global over 2 weeks with rollback hooks
